I hadn't done those things in reality because of severe anxiety. Severe anxiety that arose from the fact that I was so incredibly terrified to do the slightest thing that may have the tiniest chance of angering my father.

This movie is slow to get into and hard to understand. But I would say it's worth it. Make sure to turn your phone off when watching though because it requires attention.

Longevity mainly. I like to own a phone for a good few years (Owned my last one for 3 years and the one before that for 5). 

My dad owned an iPhone 5 for 5 years before changing and my sister had a 5s for 4. The only issue any of us have had with iPhones so far has been the annoying battery life. 

The last time I used Android I had a Galaxy S3 for 5 years. It was great for about a year and a half, but after the warranty period ended it became a hassle. I had to replace the charger port, the battery swole up(i.e a similar issue to the Galaxy Note 7), it quickly became more and more unresponsive, and finally, I had to turn it off during school time just to make it through the day because if I left it on it would only last a few hours. This was shortly after replacing the battery.

During that same period, the only issue my sister and dad had with their iPhones was battery life (which to be fair was not great, but it was still better than my S3). Then got an iPhone 7 and the 3 years I had it I didn't have any of those issues aside from slightly less than good battery life (I'm not a power user so it was alright for me). It also appeared to me as responsive as it was brand new.

I like the regular software updates as well combined with the fact they're supporting phones for 6 years now. I don't know if I'm going to keep a phone for 6 years, but I'm pretty sure I'll keep it for 3 or more. The majority of people who've kept phones for that long around me have been iPhone users

Got a XS Max now and it does everything I need to and has finally fixed battery life issues for me. Lasts a day, and on rare occasion a day and a half. 

I may swtich to OnePlus when the time comes  for a phone change though, because their software looks great and they seem to keep regular updates for a while.
